criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core admission: plan_findings on a plan with no dependents (empty list) returns a Major finding naming the missing section; an entry with a blank name, or with neither test nor reason, returns a Major finding naming that dependent; a complete section adds no finding.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: 20 passed. That includes a_plan_with_no_dependents_is_a_major_finding_naming_the_missing_section (exactly one Major finding, source Athena, location 'dependents', summary 'no dependents section'), a_dependent_with_a_blank_name_or_neither_test_nor_reason_is_a_major_finding_naming_it (a blank name gives 'Dependent 2 has a blank name'; no test or reason, including whitespace-only strings, gives a finding naming the entry's name) and a_complete_dependents_section_adds_no_finding. In the base, dependents_findings does not exist, so these assertions would fail.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a replay test for the CI-reuse case searches the real sources for the changed behaviour (exit_code) and shows the seen-commands filter in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs turns up, and the dependents requirement is unmet unless the section names that rule; the test fails if it is not named.
criteria.evidence: The full suite passed in the CI record. I ran the targeted test ci_reuse_replay_the_seen_commands_filter_turns_up_in_a_search_and_must_be_named and it passed. It walks the real athena-core/src tree for the built needle exit_code and asserts verify.rs is among the hits and still holds `c.reused && c.exit_code.is_none()`. It then asserts that dependents_unnamed leaves verify.rs unnamed for a section that omits it, and leaves it out once an entry names it.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-context and cargo test -p athena-data: PlanOutput's JSON schema includes dependents, and a stored JobPlan record without the field still deserializes (records round-trip test passes).
criteria.evidence: athena-context: 99 passed, including the_plan_schema_requires_dependents_and_a_plan_without_the_key_reads_as_empty, and the nested-object count went to 6. athena-data: plan_dependents_are_optional_in_old_records_and_round_trip_when_set passed. An old record with no key parses, re-serializes byte for byte and passes check_record_file. JobPlan.dependents is marked serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty). The full athena-data suite passed in the CI record.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md requires a 'dependents' section: for each behaviour, record, config key, check name or host setting the plan changes, list the code, rules (decisions, verdict rules, admission and gate checks) and host settings that read or rely on it, found by searching the repository and docs/system-facts.md, each with a test or a reason it is unaffected.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. planner.md adds a 'dependents (required; Athena refuses a plan without it)' bullet that contains every clause in this criterion, word for word, and also names the entry fields.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/critic.md asks, as its own question, what else this change breaks, and tells the critic to check the dependents list against a repository search.
criteria.evidence: critic.md adds its own bullet: 'What else does this change break? Take each thing the plan changes, Grep the repository for its readers, and check the plan's dependents list against what you find.' plan_body in briefs.rs now prints the Dependents block in the critic brief, and a briefs test checks it.

criteria.evidence: planner_and_critic_frames_are_short_and_fit_the_budgets passed. docs/system-facts.md now reads 'budget planner: 966 of 1300' and 'budget critic: 902 of 1300', and the CI record's full suite (which includes the system-facts budget match in athena-cli) passed.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the dependents section, its admission refusal and the critic question; docs/design/job-planning.md describes the new field.
criteria.evidence: CHANGELOG has an Unreleased/Added entry covering the section, the Major refusal in plan_findings (with no critic call), the critic's question, the root cause and the replay test. job-planning.md section 3 lists dependents in the planner output, in Athena's own checks and in the critic's checks.

criteria.criterion: The change refuses more plans than before (plans without dependents); expected 15% of newly refused readings, and the higher refusal rate is intended. Check by running cargo test -p athena-core refusal_corpus.
criteria.evidence: The command as written runs 0 tests: 'refusal_corpus' is a test binary name, not a test-name filter. The planned form, --test refusal_corpus, ran 10 tests and all passed. They include plan_side::plan_cases_get_the_expected_outcome (missing, blank-name, no-test-or-reason and whitespace cases are refused; test-only, reason-only and complete CI-reuse cases are accepted), plus the existing corpus tests, design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended among them.

findings.summary: The criterion's literal command filters by test name, so it matches no test
findings.evidence: Running `cargo test -p athena-core refusal_corpus` gave 0 tests in all three binaries. The demonstration used `--test refusal_corpus`, which runs the 10 corpus tests, and they pass. This is a fault in how the criterion was worded, not in the candidate.

findings.summary: The existing frame-size guard was loosened from 500 to 700 tokens
findings.evidence: The candidate changed `estimate_tokens(frame.text) < 500` to `< 700` to make room for the planner and critic frames. The composed sets stay well inside the 1300 budget (966 and 902), but this guard has less room left for future growth.

findings.summary: The file-name match in dependents_unnamed could give false positives for common names such as mod.rs
findings.evidence: A path counts as named when any entry's text contains its file name. Only tests call this function, and its doc comment says production does not run the search, so the risk is limited.

summary: Pass. The candidate adds a required `dependents` section to `PlanOutput` and its schema, and to the `JobPlan` record. The record field is serde-default and is not written when empty, so stored plans written before the field existed still parse. `plan_findings` now gives a Major finding when the section is empty, when an entry has a blank name or dependent, or when an entry has neither a test nor a reason. It runs only on fresh planner output, so stored plans are not re-checked. The planner prompt gains the required rule, and the critic prompt gains its own "what else does this change break" question; the critic brief now shows the dependents. The CI-reuse replay test searches the real sources and shows the seen-commands filter in verify.rs must be named. CHANGELOG, the design doc and the budget lines in docs/system-facts.md are updated. I ran the admission, ci_reuse, athena-context, athena-data plan and refusal_corpus tests in this snapshot, and all passed; fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in the CI record. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. Two minor findings: criterion 8's literal command matches no tests (the `--test refusal_corpus` form does and passes), and the frame-size guard was loosened from 500 to 700 tokens.
